statement: You are given a positive integer n. Return every positive integer that divides n exactly, in increasing order.

Divisors come in pairs: if d divides n then so does n / d, and one of the two is at most √n. So it is enough to try d from 1 to √n, keeping d and n / d for each hit (only once when d × d = n), and then put the results in order.

examples.explanation: The pairs are 1 × 36, 2 × 18, 3 × 12, 4 × 9 and 6 × 6. Since 36 is a perfect square, 6 is listed only once, giving 9 divisors.
The pairs are 1 × 12, 2 × 6 and 3 × 4, giving six divisors.
